subject.title: fix(agents-bind): generate peer format for feishu group bindings

question: Which Feishu bind grammar should OpenClaw support for conversation ids while preserving existing account-scoped binds?
rationale: The code can generate peer-shaped Feishu bindings, but choosing between two-segment reinterpretation, explicit peer syntax, or plugin-owned recognition changes a public CLI/config contract and affects upgrades.

options.title: Preserve account binds and add a safe peer path
options.body: Keep `--bind <channel>` and account-scoped Feishu binds compatible, then add either explicit peer syntax or plugin-owned Feishu conversation recognition with docs, tests, and proof.

options.title: Adopt a sibling candidate
options.body: Pause this PR and choose another open candidate if its grammar better preserves account semantics, closing the rest only after one viable fix merges.

options.title: Accept the new escape intentionally
options.body: Allow `feishu:<id>` to become peer and require `feishu:account:<id>` for accounts, but land it only with upgrade notes and maintainer-owned compatibility proof.

recommendation.title: Preserve account binds and add a safe peer path
recommendation.body: Keep `--bind <channel>` and account-scoped Feishu binds compatible, then add either explicit peer syntax or plugin-owned Feishu conversation recognition with docs, tests, and proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The account-scoped bind command surface introduced in 96c77025263d is the compatibility contract most directly affected by the grammar choice.
